newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market inches up at week-end trading.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market inches up at week-end trading.

text.p: Stocks on Cyprus' stock exchange inched up during the week with favourable prospects for a continuation of the trend until the end of the year, analysts said on Friday.
The 41-share CSE general index recouped on losses made in the first two trading days this week to close at 81.59 on Friday, up 11 basis points from last week's close.

"There has been no sign of window dressing yet," said one analyst, referring to deliberate attempts to bump up the price of publicly-quoted titles to make it look good for company books at year end, common in some markets.
"I have got no doubt we will still see it," said Nicolas Severis, chairman of Sigma-Severis and Athienitis Limited.
The advent of a new investment company, Era Split Capital is adding some momentum to the market in block trading, Severis said.
"Some institutional clients feel 1997 is a good year and they are beginning to buy gently. Window dressing and new cash will see the year ending higher," he said.
Bank of Cyprus fully paid shares closed unchanged at 339.5. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank gained 4.5 cents, closing at 331.5.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares were unchanged at 256.5. Shares in the Universal Savings Bank went down two cents closing at 132.5.
Insurance company Universal Life was trading at 370, down 4.5 cents in the week. Paneuropean Insurance at 115.5, down one cent from last week.
Interamerican Insurance closed up two cents at 102.5.
In the manufacturing sector, Vassiliko Cement closed on Friday at 163, up half a cent. The Cyprus Cement Company shed 6.5 cents to close at 253.5.
Beer and wine producer Keo closed the week at 115.5, down two cents from last Friday.
